ai.description: This slender viper reaches 70–90 cm. It is bright green above with a distinct reddish-brown tail, a white lateral stripe, and a triangular head with vertical pupils. Family: Viperidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Trimeresurus erythrurus* is best distinguished by its bright, brick-red tail, which contrasts sharply with its green body and lacks the distinct white lateral stripe found in *T. albolabris*.
ai.habitat: *Trimeresurus erythrurus* inhabits humid evergreen and deciduous forests, often frequenting bamboo thickets and riparian vegetation from sea level up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Redtail Pit Viper is primarily nocturnal, often remaining motionless for hours while waiting in ambush for unsuspecting prey to pass within striking distance.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trimeresurus erythrurus* is ovoviviparous, producing litters of 6–15 young. Mating typically occurs during the monsoon season, with births recorded in late summer or autumn.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trimeresurus erythrurus* is found in Northeast India, primarily across Assam and Mizoram, typically inhabiting low-to-mid elevation forests and scrublands.
